name: law_firm_software_011_matter_staffing_roster_reconciliation
instruction: Run the matter staffing roster reconciliation for the firm, batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta), as of the episode date. A matter's team_members roster is supposed to list everyone actually doing work on it, and the firm's referential-integrity policy (REF-INTEG-01 in firm_policies) governs which assignments count: reconcile every matter's roster against the assigned_to values on that matter's own deadlines and tasks rows, and append one entry per assigned employee the roster is missing -- the firm's contributor convention decides what the appended entry looks like (the employee's id stands in for the name until the roster is properly maintained, and the role is the firm's standard contributor role). Never remove or reorder an existing roster entry, never touch a matter whose roster already lists everyone actually assigned to it, and never append someone the active-roster rule excludes -- assignments that fail the policy's active-at-episode-date rule are a finding to diagnose, not a gap to fill. Then report what the sweep did: one ops_reports row (report='staffing_reconciliation', batch_code) with the number of matters whose roster changed and the total number of entries appended; one ops_reports row per updated matter (report='staffing_addition_detail', batch_code) derived from the post-update live roster; and one ops_reports diagnosis row per excluded assignment (report='staffing_diagnosis', batch_code) classifying it per the firm's taxonomy and naming the employee and where the assignment lives. No other ops_reports rows for this batch_code under those three report names may exist. Do not modify deadlines, tasks, or any other collection. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: 13 assignment rows (8 deadlines + 5 tasks, snapshot-confirmed) are assigned to departed EMP-006 -- staff_roster.active_to 2026-03-31 is past at any post-March-2026 episode date, so REF-INTEG-01's active-at-episode-date rule excludes them: appending EMP-006 to any matter FAILs, and sweeping them up without the required latent_organizational diagnosis also FAILs. All 13 sit on dangling matter refs (missing-matter-*), so an agent that appends by raw matter_id either no-ops or corrupts the matters collection.

the true repair set is computable only against the full ~6000-row deadlines+tasks set crossed with the seed rosters (snapshot-confirmed this rebuild: 44 matters updated, 48 entries appended, of which 25 bulk deadlines + 25 bulk tasks are deliberately planted off-team assignments deduped by matter); assuming the hand-authored gap count (matters 5/6/7) under-repairs, and appending employees with no assignment on the matter corrupts clean rosters.

the assignment scan crosses dangling and PLACEHOLDER-scaffolding matter refs (8 deadlines 'missing-matter-*', 6 dangling tasks, plus PLACEHOLDER- scaffolding exempt per REF-INTEG-01) -- an agent that 'repairs' those by creating matters or rows outside matters.team_members corrupts collections outside the blast radius (snapshot-confirmed: the matters row count must not change).

success_criteria.summary: Every matter's team_members array contains an entry for every employee actually assigned to that matter's deadlines/tasks who is active on staff_roster at the episode date, appended in the firm's contributor shape; existing entries keep their order and values byte-identical; matters with no gap are untouched; departed-staff assignments are never appended and are diagnosed as latent_organizational. One staffing_reconciliation summary row (counts recomputed from the seed snapshot, never hardcoded), one staffing_addition_detail row per updated matter from post-update live state, one staffing_diagnosis row per excluded assignment. Dual-path confirmed (raw-row vs SQL); deadlines and tasks canary-identical.

checks.expect: team_members appended only where a real assignment gap exists, existing entries preserved in order, appended entries exactly the firm's contributor convention; matters with no gap untouched
per-matter assigned-employee sets agree between the raw-row filter and a SQL UNION over deadlines/tasks
EMP-006 never appended to any matter; every departed-staff assignment carries a latent_organizational diagnosis row; acting on the near-miss (appending EMP-006) FAILs
summary counts and detail rows agree between Python-derived expectations and SQL over the written rows

checks.collection: all seeded collections outside blast_radius, including deadlines and tasks

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: v2 moves the governing rule into staff_roster + REF-INTEG-01: the agent must discover that assignments to the departed employee (active_to in the past) are excluded from the append set and must be DIAGNOSED as latent_organizational rather than appended, while the append set itself is a live cross-collection membership computation over ~6000 assignment rows against nested JSON rosters -- the only task in the suite that mutates a nested array field under an active-roster temporal rule.
